label: original-phase positions 4-6, boosted when p/r appeared at positions 1-2
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase at steps 4-6, peaking at step 5. Steps 4-6 hold 98% of activation mass. It is silent at t<=2 and in the copy phase, with a weak tail at t=3, t=7 and the <DEL> step. Within that window, whether it fires and how strongly depends on which tokens were at original positions 1-2: p and r (and to a lesser degree o) raise it. When both orig(1) and orig(2) are in {p,r}, precision is 0.98 and these steps include the strongest activations (e.g. h p r o q [h]). Position alone has F1 0.18 (recall 0.94); adding p/r at position 1 or 2 gives F1 0.50 and mass recall 0.70. Missed activations are mostly weak and spread across many token contexts, which suggests a graded sum over early tokens rather than a clean rule. Input-token identity has little effect, and first occurrences are somewhat favored.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the second original token (most: p, r, o, 3, m, k; least: w, y, e, c) and the third original token (most: p, r, o, m, 3, k; least: q, 0, e, w); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=4, t=6.
